what: Every place where the validity or availability of a ZK, privacy, FHE or proof operation depends on something other than committed State and the transaction bytes, with the operation it gates, the committed source that decides it instead (or its removal) and the plan task that owns the change. `sites` are the detector hits attributed to an entry as [path, detector, token, occurrences]; the checker fails on a hit no entry lists and on a listed hit that is gone. `attribution` says whether the entry was written from reading its code (`read`) or assigned by a path rule (`path_rule`): a path-rule entry records where a class of names occurs and which task owns that code, not a site-by-site reading. Recording a gate establishes neither its removal nor the security of the operation behind it. Limits of the scan: it reads production Rust sources of the listed crates and the listed SDK roots as text. It does not see a gate written with none of the detected names (for example a chain-identity condition that names no network in a literal and uses none of the detected identifiers), a result selected under a Cargo feature the census does not classify as a gate, a read of a node-configuration policy field through a local variable instead of a field path, or anything built by a macro. Outside the proof path, clock readings and reviewer or approval names are scanned only in Core's admission, execution, validation and publication files. Crates outside the list are not scanned.

kinds.environment: A process environment variable, or a build-time environment value.
kinds.node_local_config: Node-local configuration: a value read from this node's configuration file.
kinds.cargo_feature: A Cargo feature that compiles or selects code.
kinds.digest: A binary, source, executable, build or catalog digest used as identity.
kinds.chain_identity: A chain-ID or network condition: production versus integration, testnet versus mainnet.
kinds.readiness_qualification: A readiness certificate, a qualification signer or receipt, a reviewer signature.
kinds.activation_lifecycle: An activation transaction or bit, a lifecycle availability switch, or the typed unavailable outcome of an unfinished operation.
kinds.global_manifest: A global all-protocol manifest or a zero availability pin.
kinds.wall_clock: A wall clock or a local timeout.

statuses.open: The gate exists. The owner task removes it or moves its source into committed State.
statuses.done: Removed or moved by F.4; `tests` and `removed` are the evidence the checker holds.
statuses.unsupported: The typed error of an operation that is not implemented or not secure yet. It depends on no configuration, feature or environment and stays mandatory work of the owner; removing it must not make the operation succeed.
statuses.local_resource: A typed failure of this node's own entropy, allocator, storage, accelerator, host or platform. It is not a gate and not unfinished work: it fails a local prover or wallet call, and on the validation path it defers the local attempt and never rejects carried evidence. `tests` names the deferral tests where the owner has them.
statuses.not_a_gate: The detector hit is not a validity or availability gate; `note` says why.
statuses.out_of_plan: Outside the products of the ZK delivery plan; recorded for visibility, `note` says why.

env_read.what: A process environment variable or a build-time environment value is read.

config_env_alias.what: A node-configuration field can be set from a process environment variable.

dev_env_flag.what: A developer environment flag is consulted.

config_switch.what: An enable or assume-valid switch of the [zk] or [confidential] node configuration is read.

node_config_read.what: A service reads the [zk] or [confidential] section of the node configuration directly.

handshake_switch.what: The confidential capability a node advertises in the P2P handshake from its own configuration (`confidential.enabled`, `assume_valid`, `verifier_backend`) is read, carried or compared.

zk_settings_install.what: A complete ZK settings value, validity values included, is installed into a State. Production code installs local resources only (State::install_node_zk); the complete installer exists in test builds, so every production call site is a defect.

zk_settings_write.what: A field named `zk` (the ZK settings of a State or of a configuration value) is assigned, with `=` or a compound operator, named by the first field written below it. Production code may write local resource settings only; every other write is a defect.

pipeline_settings_install.what: A complete pipeline settings value, execution limits included, is installed into a State. Production code installs local resources only (State::install_node_pipeline); the complete installer exists in test builds, so every production call site is a defect.

pipeline_settings_write.what: A field named `pipeline` (the pipeline settings of a State or of a configuration value) is assigned, with `=` or a compound operator, named by the first field written below it. Production code may write local resource settings only; every other write is a defect.

settings_mut_borrow.what: A field named `zk` or `pipeline` is borrowed mutably (`&mut x.zk`, which is also how `mem::replace`, `mem::swap` and `mem::take` reach it) or overwritten with `clone_from`, named by the field. The settings fields of `State` are private, so outside the State modules such a line does not compile; inside them every site is listed.

default_validity_settings.what: Production code names the protocol-default verification gas schedule (`DEFAULT_ZK_GAS`) or builds a default ZK, gas or pipeline settings value (`Zk::default()`, `ConfidentialGas::default()`, `Pipeline::default()`). Metering, admission and fee bounds must take the schedule and limits frozen in the block or view they execute in; a default value passed to a meter, a host or a quote instead is a defect, so every site is listed.

node_policy_read.what: State, a block, a view or a service reads a field of the node-configuration policy sections whose validity values are not committed yet ([pipeline], [nexus], [gov], [crypto], [oracle], [fraud_monitoring], [content], [settlement]). A row is recorded when the path read is a field of one of the catalogs the resource contract records, named by the catalog field it reaches.

feature_cfg.what: Code is compiled or selected under a Cargo feature. Rows are required only for features the census classifies as validity or availability gates.

digest_identity.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names a source, binary, build, catalog or release digest. The class word starts a word of the identifier and the digest word ends one, so `resource_shape` and `ReleaseShare` do not match; a plain `commit_hash` or `commit_digest` is a commitment value and is not matched, and a builder function named `build_sha<bits>_<what>` (the verb `build` followed by a hash function and the thing built, such as `build_sha256_word_circuit_v1`) is not a build digest and is not matched.

chain_condition.what: An identifier names a production, integration, testnet, mainnet or pinned-chain condition.

chain_literal.what: A value is compared with, or matched against, a string literal that names a network (minamoto, taira, mainnet, testnet, devnet) in a crate that decides or verifies.

qualification.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names a qualification, a readiness record, a reviewer or an audit signoff. `fully_qualified` (a complete `name@domain` identifier, as in `parse_fully_qualified`) is a parsing term and is not matched.

activation.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names an activation or a lifecycle. Class `revocation_state` is derived from the source: the identifier is the name of a lifecycle enum whose variants are exactly `Active` and `Revoked`, or `Active`, `Superseded` and `Revoked`, the in-force state of a committed record. Class `constant_true` (any identifier detector) is a `const NAME: bool = true`.

unavailable.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names an unavailable, suspended or unsupported outcome. Class `local_resource` is a failure of this node's entropy, allocator, storage, accelerator, host or platform; class `version_check` is the rejection of an encoding version this release does not define; the other classes are either a gate or the accurate error of an unfinished operation.

unfinished_constant.what: A file on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path defines a `bool` constant set to `false` whose name says that something is available, implemented, qualified, ready, supported, wired, complete, verified or integrated: the compile-time record of an unfinished step, which the code that reads it turns into a refusal or a not-ready status.

global_manifest.what: An identifier names the Exact12 catalog, a capability or release manifest, or an availability pin.

wall_clock.what: A wall clock or an elapsed-time reading on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path.

core_wall_clock.what: A wall clock or an elapsed-time reading in Core's admission, execution, validation and publication files that are not on the proof path (the `wall_clock` detector covers those that are).

core_review_gate.what: An identifier in Core's admission, execution, validation and publication files that are not on the proof path names a reviewer, a signoff, an audit certificate or an approval.

time_budget.what: An identifier on the ZK, privacy, FHE or proof path names a timeout, a deadline or a millisecond budget. Class `height_deadline` is a deadline expressed as a block height or epoch, which is committed State and not a clock. Class `deadline_outcome` names the outcome of a deadline that has passed (`...DeadlineExpired`), a failure kind recorded from committed State.

sdk_availability.what: An SDK source names a qualification, a readiness record, a capability or release manifest or the Exact12 catalog (one row per file and class).

entries.gates: Every limit, window, verifier switch, relation-selecting verifying-key identity (Kaigi authorization and usage) and verification gas charge bound by compute_zk_consensus_policy_hash: Halo2 and STARK proof and envelope sizes, max_k, batch, SCCP proof and verifier-work limits, proof retention, bridge-proof windows, confidential anchor age and policy-transition windows, registry caps and the confidential gas schedule.
entries.decided_by: The committed custom parameter `zk_validity_policy_v1` (type, protocol default and canonical structural and coherence validation in iroha_data_model; application to State in iroha_core::zk_validity_policy). An ordinary authorized `SetParameter` installs or changes it, in genesis or later; block construction freezes the policy of the predecessor's committed parameters, so a change governs the next block and the genesis block runs under the protocol default. Executor data-model reconciliation never writes it. A node installs local resources only (State::install_node_zk) and its configuration schema has no validity field (cfg.zk.node_schema).
entries.note: Verification gas is metered with the schedule frozen in each block's settings; no process-wide schedule exists (gas.process_wide_schedule, done). The two enable switches are committed fields that the plan author decided to delete (switch.zk.backend_enabled).

entries.gates: The validity-affecting keys of the `[zk]` and `[confidential]` sections of the node configuration: `[zk.stark]`, `[zk.sccp]`, the limits, curve, backend and switch of `[zk.halo2]`, the scalar `[zk]` caps, windows and key references, the `[confidential]` limits and windows and `[confidential.gas]`.
entries.decided_by: Removed from the node schema: a configuration that names one fails to load with the ordinary aggregated unknown-parameter error. The sections keep local resource settings only (verifier workers, queues and budgets, FASTPQ prover settings, `confidential.verify_timeout_ms`). The tracked Taira configuration and the built-in `sora-nexus-v1` profile no longer carry such keys.
entries.note: `confidential.enabled`, `assume_valid` and `verifier_backend` remain (cfg.confidential.node_switches).

entries.gates: The confidential policy hash a genesis header binds. Genesis generators (kagami `genesis sign` and `prepared`, the iroha_deploy localnet and private-root builders, the test network) hashed the authoring node configuration into it, while validation computes it from State.
entries.decided_by: Every generator signs the protocol-default hash (default_genesis_confidential_policy_hash): the genesis block runs under the protocol default on every validator. A chain authors other values only as the `zk_validity_policy_v1` parameter of its genesis manifest, as the tracked Taira template does. The function that hashes a settings value is crate-internal.

entries.gates: 23 `ZK_*` process environment variables that set validity-affecting [zk] fields of the node configuration (proof and envelope sizes, max_k, batch, enable switches, curve, backend, history caps, bridge-proof windows, parameter-set identifiers).
entries.decided_by: Removed: the fields have no environment alias. Their values are committed chain policy (cfg.zk.validity_policy).

entries.gates: Environment aliases of local ZK verifier-lane resources (worker threads, queue and retry capacities, enqueue wait, wall-clock budget) and of the FASTPQ prover (execution mode, device selection, Metal tuning).
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: a local resource may only defer.
entries.note: None of these fields is bound by compute_zk_consensus_policy_hash; the test local_resources_survive_and_never_move_the_consensus_hash pins the split, and policy_of names every field of the settings value as policy or local resource.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of local resource fields in the [pipeline], [gov] and [fraud_monitoring] sections.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local.
entries.note: Read alias by alias. The eighteen PIPELINE_* aliases other than PIPELINE_GAS_TECH_ACCOUNT_ID set fields that `pipeline_validity_policy::policy_of` marks as local resources (access-set cache, caches, tracing, GPU bucket, prover threads, parallel apply and overlay, the default cursor mode, the ready-queue heap, signature batch sizes, the stateless cache and workers); every execution limit of [pipeline] lost its key and alias (cfg.pipeline.node_schema). GOV_DEBUG_TRACE_PIPELINE and GOV_ALIAS_FRONTIER_TELEMETRY switch tracing and telemetry, and FRAUD_MONITORING_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS / FRAUD_MONITORING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS bound this node's calls to its fraud service; none of the four is a field of the execution-policy digest.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of the inputs that say which chain a node joins: CHAIN, CHAIN_DISCRIMINANT, GENESIS_EXPECTED_HASH, GENESIS_EXPECTED_HASH_FILE, GENESIS_MANIFEST_JSON and GENESIS_PUBLIC_KEY.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: an operator names the chain and pins its genesis.
entries.note: They select and authenticate the genesis a node starts from. A node with another value follows another chain or refuses to start; within one chain every rule comes from that signed genesis and the State committed after it. They are not a production-versus-integration condition: no code compares them with a network name.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of validity-affecting node-configuration fields that are not committed yet: the governance policy (GOV_* voting, bond, slashing, council and viral incentive fields), the admitted algorithms (CRYPTO_*), the Nexus fee asset and sink (NEXUS_FEE_*), the oracle history depth, the fraud-monitoring switch and grace, the fee account PIPELINE_GAS_TECH_ACCOUNT_ID and COMPUTE_ENABLED.
entries.decided_by: Committed State for every one of these fields (cfg.governance, cfg.crypto.algorithms, cfg.oracle_fraud, cfg.nexus.policy, cfg.pipeline.gas_identity). A committed field keeps no key and no environment alias.
entries.note: Read alias by alias against the fields of the execution-policy digest and the Nexus policy preimage. COMPUTE_ENABLED is listed here because its field enables the compute lane; the digest does not bind it and its owner decides whether it is a service switch.
entries.open_reason: Removing an alias is only meaningful together with the move of its field into committed State; those moves are the open cfg.* entries. The committed-parameter mechanism exists (zk_validity_policy_v1). This family still reaches validation through the State copy installed from node configuration at startup; moving it needs its own typed committed parameter, the staged-genesis and deployment generators that author it, and regenerated deployment configurations.

entries.gates: Environment aliases of local service settings: Torii, P2P, Connect, logging, telemetry, snapshots, tiered storage, concurrency, NTS, ISO bridge, Norito codec, keys and addresses.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: transport, storage, observability and identity of this process.
entries.note: Attributed by prefix. A validity-affecting field added under one of these prefixes would need its own entry.

entries.gates: `confidential.enabled`, `confidential.assume_valid` and `confidential.verifier_backend` of the node configuration: a validator refuses to start without confidential verification, an observer may accept confidential blocks without verifying them, and the three values are advertised and compared in the P2P handshake (ConfidentialHandshakeCaps; a mismatch is HandshakeConfidentialMismatch).
entries.decided_by: Delete (plan-author decision of this task): verification implementations ship unconditionally and supported proofs are always verified; an observer that does not verify is not a mode of this release. The handshake keeps the release-bound confidential feature digest only (the rules version and the protocol-default policy hash; it reads no State since this change).
entries.open_reason: Deleting them changes the P2P handshake record, its comparison and its tests in iroha_p2p, the validator start checks of irohad and the localnet, test-network, profile and Taira configurations that write the keys. The handshake record is pinned field by field as protocol carrier `peer_handshake` in crates/iroha_core/src/state/state_table_inventory_tests.rs and specs/state_table_inventory.json (`ConfidentialHandshakeCaps.assume_valid`, `.verifier_backend`, `HandshakeConfidentialMeta.assume_valid`, `.verifier_backend`), files of G.1/BH.3 that are being edited in this wave and that F.4 may not change; the deletion is filed as a shared-file request for the integration pass. It is not a validity change of a validator (which must already run with enabled=true, assume_valid=false). TODO(F.4) at the handshake caps in irohad and at the schema fields in iroha_config.

entries.gates: Reads and writes of `config.zk` outside the configuration crate: the daemon installing local resources into State (install_node_zk), starting the local diagnostic ZK lane from the node's own verifier settings, FASTPQ prover selection, device labels and the compatibility probe; the staged-genesis builder and the test network installing the same local resources; and the localnet builder passing the settings value to the execution-policy digest.
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: the settings value a configuration produces holds this node's local resources and the protocol-default validity values, because the node schema has no validity field (cfg.zk.node_schema).
entries.note: Negative test: installs_actual_zk_and_settlement_config_before_kura_replay (irohad) asserts that an SCCP limit placed in a settings value by hand does not reach State. The writes are `config.zk.fastpq.*` assignments of the daemon's FASTPQ command-line overrides.

entries.gates: `halo2.enabled` and `stark.enabled`: proof verification, verifying-key registration and the host ZK syscalls reject a backend whose switch is off (world.rs, ivm/host.rs, executor.rs), and Torii's prover worker skips it.
entries.decided_by: Delete (plan-author decision of this task): both verifiers are always on. Until then the switches are fields of the committed policy (cfg.zk.validity_policy) with the protocol default `true`, so two validators cannot differ and no node configuration can turn one off.
entries.open_reason: Deleting the two fields changes the preimage of compute_zk_consensus_policy_hash, that is the confidential feature digest of every block header, and the ZK term of the execution-policy digest signed into genesis. It is an incompatible change of the `genesis` and `execution_semantics` surfaces: the pinned first-release history is regenerated and the cutover declared in the same change (specs/first_release_history_cutover.json, owned by BH.2 in this wave), and the authority-registry projection (state/authority_registry/zk_policy.rs, G.1) and the `zk-stark` feature gate (feature.zk_stark) change with it. Not done in this change; TODO(F.4) at the two fields in iroha_data_model::zk_validity_policy.

entries.gates: Any writer of the State-owned ZK or pipeline settings other than the installers: a mutable borrow, `mem::replace`, `mem::swap`, `clone_from` or an assignment from another module or crate.
entries.decided_by: The fields `State::zk` and `State::pipeline` are private. Code outside the State modules reads local resources through `State::installed_zk` and `State::installed_pipeline` and validity values through `zk_snapshot`, `pipeline_snapshot`, a view or a block; it cannot name the fields, so the installers (`install_node_zk`, `install_node_pipeline`) are the only production writers by construction. Test builds add `edit_zk_for_testing` and `edit_pipeline_for_testing`, which install the edited value through `set_zk` and `set_pipeline`. The one mutable borrow the scan finds, `block_zk: &mut fields.zk` in state.rs, hands the frozen settings copy of a block to its transaction; it is a field of `StateBlock`, not the State-owned value. Making the fields private exposed one reader of the installed value where the committed policy was meant: Torii's proof-retention status now reads `zk_snapshot()`.

entries.gates: A protocol-default verification gas schedule or default settings value used where the schedule or limits frozen in a block or view must be used.
entries.decided_by: Every production site is listed and the scan fails on a new one. gas.rs defines `DEFAULT_ZK_GAS`, the protocol default as a constant for tests, benches and the State-free overlay builder. The three `CoreHost` constructors in smartcontracts/ivm/host.rs start with it and `set_zk_config` replaces it with the block's frozen schedule for every State-backed host. `staged_default_pipeline` in crates/iroha_deploy builds the pipeline settings of genesis staging, and the genesis block runs under the protocol default. No meter, admission or fee-quote call passes the constant: queue admission and the fee bound are tested under a committed schedule that differs from it, on a node that installed a third one.

entries.gates: Every assignment to the State-owned pipeline settings value or to a field below it.
entries.decided_by: No assignment writes an execution limit. The whole value is stored by the private `install_pipeline_settings`, reached in production only through `State::install_node_pipeline`, which strips validity values first (`node_local_resources`). The test-fixture constructor (`configure_test_runtime_defaults`) writes four local scheduling settings (`parallel_apply`, `parallel_overlay`, `ready_queue_heap`, `workers`). The executor writes the per-transaction copy of the fee policy `pipeline.gas` (`tech_account_id`, `accepted_assets`, `units_per_gas`) and fee settlement restores the copy captured at admission; that family is cfg.pipeline.gas_identity. `State::set_pipeline` exists in test builds only, and the scan reports any new install or write (detectors pipeline_settings_install, pipeline_settings_write).

entries.gates: Confidential verification gas was metered from one process-wide schedule (ZK_GAS_BASE_VERIFY and four more) rather than from the ZK settings a block froze.
entries.decided_by: The schedule is an argument of the meter: `meter_instruction`, `meter_instructions`, `confidential_gas_cost` and `sum_confidential_gas_costs` take the verification gas schedule of the executing block (`StateBlock::zk.gas`, the committed `zk_validity_policy_v1` or the protocol default). The executor and trigger execution pass the transaction's frozen settings, the IVM host the settings it was configured with for the block, queue admission and the fee quotes the schedule of the view they read. The five process statics, their installers and the test lock are deleted; two States with different committed schedules run in one process. Torii's configuration record, the telemetry gauges and `iroha confidential gas get` report the schedule State charges.

entries.gates: Torii's private-settlement route controller is created from an environment variable naming a control directory (Controller::from_env); the module belongs to the `test-network-private-settlement-route-control` feature surface.
entries.decided_by: Remove from production builds, or keep strictly as a test-network fault-injection hook that cannot be compiled into a validator release.

entries.gates: Torii's attachment sanitizer child process recognizes its role and its input bound from three environment variables set by the parent Torii process.
entries.decided_by: Stays local: process-role plumbing of a local sandbox; attachments are node-local worker input, not consensus evidence.
entries.note: The parent sets the variables itself; an operator environment does not select a behavior.

entries.gates: Build-time environment values (git commit, Cargo features, target triple) compiled into the release identity a node reports.
entries.decided_by: Stays evidence metadata.
entries.note: Build provenance reported by status and diagnostics. The census records it so that a comparison of this identity in admission would be noticed as a new site.

entries.gates: Developer environment flags that disable or force-fail the Metal and CUDA self-tests (IVM_DISABLE_METAL, IVM_FORCE_METAL_SELFTEST_FAIL, IVM_DEBUG_METAL_SELFTEST, CUDA trace).
entries.decided_by: Stays local: acceleration selection. Every accelerated path has a scalar fallback with identical results; M.2 and M.3 own the parity evidence.
entries.note: The flags are consulted through dev_env_flag; they select between equivalent implementations and never a different result.

entries.gates: The FASTPQ GPU backend reads `SystemRoot` to locate system libraries on Windows.
entries.decided_by: Stays local: library discovery of a local prover accelerator.
entries.note: Prover-side only.

entries.gates: The ZK-X509 diagnostic prover reads its output directory and a public candidate selector from the environment.
entries.decided_by: Stays local: a measurement harness (E.1), not admission.
entries.note: engine_prover_diagnostic.rs produces measurements; the verifier path reads no environment.

entries.gates: Every Exact12 privacy submission: PrivacyProtocolRegistryV1::active_record returns a protocol only when its PrivacyProtocolActivationRecordV1 is in lifecycle state Active, which requires an explicit governed activation transition.
entries.decided_by: Remove the activation record and lifecycle. A supported canonical profile with valid cryptography, permissions, committed key policy, replay and resource limits is usable once registered.

entries.gates: Privacy proof admission resolves a protocol only through the singleton PrivacyExact12QualificationRecordV1 (World cell privacy_exact12_qualification): an all-twelve qualification record signed for a release.
entries.decided_by: Remove. No all-protocol qualification record; each implemented protocol is valid independently by its own committed relation and keys.

entries.gates: Privacy protocol activation is validated against the compiled-profile catalog of the running binary (artifact and profile digests compiled into privacy_profiles.rs).
entries.decided_by: A semantic relation and parameter identity in committed State. P.1 makes the native dispatch the single owner; compiled digests stay build metadata.

entries.gates: ZK-X509 activation requires compiled readiness (zk_x509_activation_readiness_v1 and the readiness certificates of profile/readiness_certificates.rs).
entries.decided_by: Per-proof relation, parameter and resource validity of the completed maximum transport (X.2 to X.4); no readiness certificate.

entries.gates: Standalone ZK ballot and tally instructions always fail with STANDALONE_ZK_RELATION_UNQUALIFIED_V1: the ballot relation that proves anonymous credential authorization and a committee-free tally does not exist yet.
entries.decided_by: The complete private election relation (P.8). The error depends on no configuration, feature or environment.

entries.gates: SoraCloud BFV full-bootstrap execution requires a release audit package signed by a trusted reviewer key (fhe_bfv.rs, soracloud/fhe.rs, isi/soracloud.rs).
entries.decided_by: Remove the reviewer signature as a prerequisite. The secure RNS-BGV replacement (C.3, C.8) with its complete proof decides validity; the known-insecure exact profile keeps a typed rejection.

entries.gates: Static classification of proof backend labels (verify, production-claim, trusted-setup, developer-only) used by verifying-key registration and proof verification.
entries.decided_by: Stays a compile-time protocol rule: identical in every binary; no chain identity or configuration is consulted.
entries.note: The detector matches the word `production` in the function names. The functions take only the backend label.

entries.gates: The local ZK lane drops a queued diagnostic task after a wall-clock enqueue wait (ingress_enqueue_timeout, dispatch_enqueue_timeout).
entries.decided_by: Stays node-local: the lane checks IVM diagnostic traces in the background for telemetry.
entries.note: The module states that the lane does not mutate WSV, is intended purely for diagnostics and telemetry, and captures records without changing execution admission (pipeline/zk_lane.rs, module documentation and capture_and_submit). A dropped task loses a diagnostic report; no transaction is deferred, rejected or accepted by it. The daemon starts the lane from the node's own verifier settings.

entries.gates: String literals that name a network, compared or matched in the crates that decide or verify.
entries.decided_by: Committed State already decides it.
entries.note: Two sites, neither a condition on this chain's own identity. `SccpNetwork::from_profile_key` (iroha_data_model/src/bridge/sccp.rs) parses the closed V1 inventory of SCCP counterparty networks from their canonical profile keys. `kura/lane_geometry.rs` compares the schema tag of an operator-written marker file of the Taira public-reset tooling; it selects a store path on this node, not a proof rule.

entries.gates: Wall-clock and elapsed-time readings in Core's block, transaction, State and publication files that are not on the proof path.
entries.decided_by: Committed State already decides it.
